lucas: Heads up 026-06-01->2026-07-15 I'll be embedded with a client in Dubai for ~45 days. Company will cover apartment and flights. Quick questions: 1) Do I need to change homebase? 2) Is the $100/month WFH stipend paused or prorated? 3) Can People Ops ship my company laptop directly to Dubai? 4) Any tax/reporting nasties I should know about for payroll? @people-ops-global @jamal (Payroll) @legal-bot @travel-team
people-ops-global: Nice, congrats on the engagement. Short answers: if you remain on Redwood payroll and the stay is temporary (<90 days), you generally do not change homebase. WFH stipend is based on your primary home workspace and is prorated for months when you're not physically working from home >50% business days. Laptop shipping is doable but needs asset tracking + customs guidance. Payroll/legal will advise on tax/immigration. Please submit the "Temporary Location Declaration" in Workday and select Dubai as the temporary address.
lucas: I'm US-based (CA resident). We'll stay on Redwood payroll. Travel team will book the apartment. If People Ops ships laptop, do I need to sign customs paperwork? Does that create a relocation event?
travel-team: We can book & ship. For shipments: if the laptop is company-owned and returning after the assignment, it's typically treated as company equipment (not relocation). You'll need to sign the courier receipt and the asset will be logged to your employee record. For customs, the courier uses temporary import documentation  ATA Carnet or carnet-like process depending on local rules. We'll coordinate with Legal for documentation.
jamal (Payroll): UAE has no personal income tax, but for US citizens/residents US tax still applies (worldwide income). Since you'll remain on Redwood payroll, standard US withholding continues. We need the Workday temp location to flag the payroll record. Social security: we need to confirm if any bilateral totalization agreement applies; likely not with UAE. Company-paid lodging could be a taxable fringe in certain jurisdictions; we'll consult tax counsel. For stipend: policy prorates monthly WFH allowance by calendar days at home vs on assignment.
legal-bot: Immigration note: Dubai/UAE allows short business visits, but "working" onsite can be considered employment activity. For 45 days, Legal wants a short description of duties for the client (meetings, hands-on pairing, demo support, or billable delivery?) before confirming whether a work permit/service visa is needed. Please attach statement in the Workday form or DM Legal.
finance-bot: Expense coding: use `TRAVEL_SHORTSTAY_DXB` for company-funded apartments up to 90 days. If People Ops pays vendor directly, Finance needs a PO and vendor tax forms. Company-paid lodging may require gross-up depending on tax treatment; get pre-approval.
lucas: Got it. One more: if the apartment covers internet, do I lose the $100 WFH stipend for that month? I still want the stipend to cover mobile hotspot costs when back home.
people-ops-global: If you're away >50% of business days in that stipend month and the company covers lodging + internet, we pause that month's stipend and prorate. If internet isn't provided or you're paying for a personal hotspot while traveling, submit receipts and we'll review exceptions.
lucas: Filing the Temporary Location Declaration now and adding the scope-of-work note for Legal. Thanks all for the fast responses :thumbsup:
